messages:
ci-bot: perf-ci: PR #9934 failed microbench thresholds for eng-runtime/batch_sampler_p50. Delta +13.2% vs main. Artifact: https://ci.redwood/internal/9934/perf.html

olivia: :eyes: saw the CI alert. which part of the PR touches batching heuristics?

raj: PR 9934 modifies the batch sampler: sampling window increased 50ms -> 200ms and made sampling stochastic (seeded RNG removed). it also touches the warmup gating.

tim: repro locally on a T4 with the perf harness:
```
./tools/bench micro --bench batch_sampler --model small-1 --iterations 2000 --seed 42
# sample output
p50: 48.1 tok/s (baseline 57.2)
p95: 98ms
```
I see the p50 jump ~15% intermittently.

olivia: can you paste the exact command + the small profiler snippet from the CI artifact?

tim: posting the minimal repro cmd + perf-stats from my run:
```
# run
./tools/bench micro --bench batch_sampler --seq-dist mix_short_long --iterations 2500 --seed 2026 --kv-cache-enabled
# perf-stats (aggregated)
batch_assemble_wait_ms: mean=12.4 p50=2.3 p95=180.4 p99=420.1
kv_cache_hitrate: 0.63
net_send_ms: mean=1.2
```
Notice the huge p95/p99 (180ms/420ms) in batch_assemble_wait — that's the culprit.

dmitri: I inspected the flamegraph from the CI artifact — long tails are dominated by sampler.wait_for_batch + sampler.random_sleep. Looks like occasionally the sampler waits the full 200ms when traffic mix produces a long string of short requests and kv-miss paths trigger an extra wait.

eva: fwiw PR 9900 last week adjusted kvcache eviction -> lowered warmup threshold; that could amplify short-request frequency and interact poorly with a larger sampling window.

raj: good catch. two candidate causes: 1) the increased sampling window (200ms) causes rare but long assembly waits; 2) removal of deterministic seed makes samplers non-reproducible and harder for CI golden runs. we should bisect between commits from 9900 and 9934.

olivia: options: quick revert of PR 9934 to unblock rollouts, or a minimal hotfix that caps max sampler wait and restores deterministic seeding for CI. which is lower risk?

tim: i prepared a small patch on fix/sampler-cap-9934 that does: cap_wait_ms = min(config.max_wait_ms, 100) and reintroduces deterministic seed when perf harness env var PERF_DETERMINISTIC=1. bench locally on T4: p50 delta ~+0.6% vs main (within threshold).

raj: can you push that as a try-run? i'll queue a CI perf re-run and a binary bisect concurrently.

ci-bot: perf-ci: queued try job for branch fix/sampler-cap-9934 (try-run id 9934-try-1). link: https://ci.redwood/internal/9934/try/1

olivia: :thumbsup: if try-run is green and microbench deltas < 1% we can merge. assign merge to @raj and add a rollout canary (10% Dedicated) afterwards. also add a short perf test that exercises short-heavy seq distributions.

dmitri: i'll add unit tests for batch assembly edgecases and a perf-case with skewed short-seq traffic to the PR.

eva: i'll update the release notes and add an entry to the rollout-blockers doc: "sampler-window change caused intermittent p99 assembly waits; hotfix applied".

raj: on it. plan: run the bisect; if bisect points clearly to 9934, ship hotfix. if bisect implicates interaction with 9900, we may revert 9900 instead. will report back in this thread after CI completes.

olivia: thanks team. acceptance criteria: try-run green, p50 delta <= 1%, p95/p99 assembly waits < 50ms. revert if not achieved.

ci-bot: perf-ci: try-run 9934-try-1 completed -> status: pending analysis (artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/9934/try/1/perf.html)

raj: assigned to me. ETA for results ~30m.

(threads/next steps pinned)
